scams.name: Manaus (MAO) Airport Taxi & Late-Night Transfer Overcharge
scams.description: Manaus International Airport (Aeroporto Eduardo Gomes, IATA MAO) sits 14 km north of Centro Histórico and 11 km north of Ponta Negra (the main tourist district). Limited late-night rideshare supply + predatory 'Special Taxi' kiosks create a systematic overcharge pattern. Community reports document 2025 general-safety context, the national airport-transfer pattern, and a coordinated Amazonas-state Uber-scam pattern (originally documented in neighbouring Pará at Santarém and Alto do Chão but translates directly to Manaus). Manaus-specific community threads cover both airport transfers and multi-day Amazon tours. Legitimate cost in 2026: Uber / 99 from MAO to Ponta Negra R$ 45–R$ 75 (30 min); to Centro Histórico R$ 35–R$ 60 (25 min); to Tropical Manaus Ecoresort R$ 50–R$ 80 (30 min). Budget public option: the Executivo MAO-Centro bus is R$ 17.30 per person (60 min to Centro), runs 5 AM–11 PM. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) 'Special Taxi' kiosks INSIDE MAO terminal quote R$ 150–R$ 280 flat to Ponta Negra — real R$ 45–R$ 75 via Uber; (b) curbside taxi touts at arrivals gate offering 'only R$ 180 to your hotel, meter broken' — no meter and real app-cost is 3x less; (c) late-night (after 11 PM) Uber wait times at MAO spike to 20–35 min because of low rideshare supply in northern Amazonas — unlicensed 'moto-taxi' mototaxistas fill the gap; (d) Uber / 99 driver demands cash top-up R$ 50–R$ 100 after pickup 'because it's too far' — cancel + rebook; (e) 'city-tour transfer' upsell at arrivals — 'R$ 300 airport + Teatro Amazonas + lunch + Ponta Negra drop-off' (real: do it yourself with Uber for R$ 80 total); (f) for returns to MAO, some Manaus hotels add a 30–50% mark-up on pre-booked transfers (hotel R$ 180, real Uber R$ 45–R$ 75); (g) unlicensed 'mototáxis' at the arrivals level offering R$ 40 fixed — NEVER use these with luggage or after dark in Manaus. For travellers: (1) book Uber / 99 on airport Wi-Fi AFTER luggage — meet driver at the official 'Aplicativos' pickup zone at Terminal 2 arrivals level (signposted); (2) for late-night arrivals (after 11 PM), pre-book a transfer via your hotel or Amazon Tours Transfer at R$ 120–R$ 180 fixed — worth it to avoid app-wait frustration in an unfamiliar city; (3) IGNORE every 'Special Taxi' kiosk inside the terminal quoting R$ 150+ — those are the overcharge operation; (4) NEVER use an unlicensed 'mototaxi' with luggage or after dark — Manaus has documented 2024–2025 mototaxi-robbery incidents per community safety reports; (5) for return to MAO, pre-book Uber the night before — saves 30 min of hotel-pickup friction; (6) if your Uber driver demands cash top-up, refuse politely + cancel in-app + rebook; use the in-app safety button if pressure escalates; (7) some hotels push their own 'transfer service' at 30–50% mark-up — DECLINE and book Uber directly from the hotel lobby on the hotel Wi-Fi; (8) DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373 (Polícia Turística Amazonas, some English); Polícia Militar 190, SAMU 192.
scams.avoidance: Uber / 99 from MAO to Ponta Negra R$ 45–R$ 75; to Centro R$ 35–R$ 60 Late-night: pre-book Amazon Tours Transfer / hotel transfer R$ 120–R$ 180 fixed NEVER use unlicensed mototaxi with luggage / after dark (robbery-incident pattern) Meet driver at 'Aplicativos' pickup zone Terminal 2 — ignore Special Taxi kiosks DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373; Polícia Militar 190
scams.location: Aeroporto Eduardo Gomes (MAO), arrivals hall, curbside

scams.name: Amazon Jungle Lodge Booking Fraud & Commission-Stop Day-Trip Scam
scams.description: The Amazon jungle lodge / river-cruise industry around Manaus has a documented commission-markup + booking-fraud ecosystem, and is the MOST common tourist complaint against the city. Community reports in 2025 extensively discuss how to tell which Manaus Amazon tour is legit or not, publish operator recommendations, and surface trip reports for both ethical operators and positive experiences. Older community threads document the same booking-fraud pattern. Legitimate 2026 cost ranges: 3-day / 2-night Amazon jungle lodge (all-inclusive — transfer, lodge, meals, 3 daily activities) is R$ 1,800–R$ 3,500 per person via reputable operators (Juma Amazon Lodge, Anavilhanas Jungle Lodge, Uacari Lodge, Amazon Eco Park Lodge, Tariri Amazon Lodge). 4–5-day trips R$ 3,000–R$ 6,000 per person. Day-trip Encontro das Águas + piranha fishing + Amazônia village R$ 250–R$ 400 per person (group, 8–10 hours). Private 2-person Encontro das Águas speedboat R$ 1,200–R$ 1,800 total. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) airport tour-desk / hotel lobby selling 'exclusive 3-night lodge package R$ 8,500 per person' with commission markup 2–3x real rate; (b) WhatsApp + Instagram 'operator' demanding PIX deposit for a lodge that doesn't exist — classic Brazilian PIX-irreversible fraud; (c) day-trip 'Encontro das Águas + tour' that becomes 3 commission stops (artisanal market, 'traditional village' for R$ 100 entry, a 'pink-dolphin swim' with captive animals R$ 200 upsell) with little actual Encontro time; (d) unlicensed 'jungle guide' offering 'authentic off-grid R$ 500 per day' without insurance, radio, or Marinha registration — documented 2024 fatalities; (e) fake 'eco-lodge' operators on booking.com with cloned reviews from legitimate lodges — verify lodge NAME on Marinha do Brasil registered-vessel list; (f) 'pink-dolphin feeding village' attraction — animal-welfare prohibited since 2025; operators still selling to unaware tourists; (g) 'wild Amazon tribe visit R$ 600' — indigenous-contact tourism is FUNAI-regulated and requires permits; most 'tribe visits' are staged performances in commercialised Amazônia villages; (h) lodge 'surprise extras' on checkout — additional R$ 400–R$ 800 for 'generator fuel' / 'kitchen staff tip' / 'cleaning fee' not disclosed on booking. For travellers: (1) BOOK direct with RECOGNISED Amazon lodges via their OFFICIAL websites — reputable: Juma Amazon Lodge (jumalodge.com), Anavilhanas Jungle Lodge (anavilhanaslodge.com), Uacari Lodge (uacari.com), Amazon Eco Park Lodge, Tariri Amazon Lodge — all with verified Marinha registration + FUNAI compliance; (2) Read Tripadvisor + Google reviews for the LODGE NAME — cross-check recent 2024–2025 reviews mentioning the specific operational details (room amenities, exact itinerary, named guides) not just generic 'amazing experience' 5-star copy-paste; (3) AVOID every 'hotel lobby R$ 8,500 exclusive package' upsell — commission markup 2–3x; (4) NEVER PIX-transfer deposit to Instagram / WhatsApp operators — only pay via credit card to verified operator websites (card chargebacks give you recourse; PIX doesn't); (5) for day-trips, book through your hotel's partnered operator (Gero Tours, Viverde, Amazonastur) at R$ 250–R$ 400 group — confirm NO commission stops in writing BEFORE booking; (6) REFUSE every 'pink-dolphin feeding' or 'wild tribe visit' — both are animal-welfare or FUNAI-regulation violations; reputable lodges do NOT offer these; (7) for travellers, 3-night at one reputable lodge (Juma / Anavilhanas / Amazon Eco Park) is the gold-standard experience — slower pace, proper guided rainforest walks, better nutrition than multi-day boat trips; (8) confirm the lodge's Marinha do Brasil boat registration BEFORE booking — legitimate operators will share the vessel number on request; (9) AMAZONASTUR (state tourism board) +55 92 2123 8800 for operator verification; DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373.
scams.avoidance: Book DIRECT via official lodge websites: Juma / Anavilhanas / Uacari / Amazon Eco Park / Tariri Verify Marinha registration + FUNAI compliance + 2024–2025 specific Tripadvisor reviews Use CREDIT CARD only (not PIX) for deposit — enables chargeback recourse Day-trips: book via hotel-partnered Gero Tours / Viverde / Amazonastur R$ 250–R$ 400 group AMAZONASTUR +55 92 2123 8800 to verify any operator; DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373
scams.location: Manaus hotel lobbies, airport tour-desks, online travel sites, Ponta Negra tour-office strip

scams.name: Encontro das Águas Boat-Tour Overcharge & Unlicensed-Operator Safety Risk
scams.description: Encontro das Águas (Meeting of the Waters — where the black Rio Negro meets the café-au-lait Rio Solimões to form the Amazon proper, 10 km downstream of Manaus) is the flagship half-day or full-day boat excursion, and hosts a parallel overcharge + unlicensed-operator risk pattern. Community reports cover 2025 excursion advice, operator verification, the broader operator landscape, and first-person trip reports from the Amazon. Legitimate 2026 cost: full-day Encontro das Águas + Janauari Ecological Park (mangroves, piranha fishing, village visit, lunch) via Gero Tours / Viverde / Amazonastur group boat R$ 250–R$ 400 per person (8 hours, includes lunch + 30–50 pax boat). Private small-group speedboat for 2–4 passengers R$ 1,200–R$ 1,800 total. The Encontro das Águas confluence itself is a 60–90 minute stop; most of the day is transit + Janauari Park activities. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Porto de Manaus tout selling 'VIP private speedboat Encontro R$ 2,500' to a single couple (real private 2-pax R$ 1,200–R$ 1,800); (b) 'helicopter Encontro tour R$ 4,500 per person' (real boat R$ 250–R$ 400 is sufficient — the confluence visual is at water level not air); (c) unlicensed speedboats at Ponta Negra pier offering R$ 800 private — no life jackets, no Marinha registration, no radio, no insurance; Amazonas river has documented capsize + engine-failure risk; (d) 'pink dolphin swim R$ 300 extra' upsell — animal-welfare prohibited since 2025 per IBAMA decree; reputable operators do NOT offer this; (e) 'mandatory environmental tax R$ 150' demanded at Janauari Park entrance (real R$ 25 Parque Estadual do Rio Negro entry); (f) 'lunch R$ 250 mandatory' on the boat (real: reputable group-tour price R$ 250–R$ 400 INCLUDES lunch — don't pay extra); (g) unlicensed boat operator 'piranha fishing R$ 100 extra' (standard group tour includes piranha fishing + bait); (h) Centro Histórico tout selling 'speedboat direct from the port R$ 400 without tour stops' — these are unregulated transfers that may skip Janauari and return in 3 hours vs the advertised 8. For travellers: (1) book group tour via your hotel's partnered operator (Gero Tours / Viverde / Amazonastur) at R$ 250–R$ 400 per person — CONFIRM the itinerary in writing (departure time, Encontro stop duration, Janauari activities, lunch, return time); (2) VERIFY the boat's Marinha do Brasil registration sticker BEFORE boarding — legitimate operators display it on the pilothouse; unlicensed vessels are a safety risk on the Amazonas; (3) CHECK life jackets for every passenger BEFORE departure — legitimate operators have them on board; refuse to board if life jackets are not provided; (4) REFUSE every 'helicopter Encontro tour' upsell — the confluence is visually best at water level; helicopter at 2,000m misses the colour contrast; (5) REFUSE every 'pink-dolphin swim' offer — illegal since 2025 IBAMA decree; reputable operators decline this; (6) REFUSE 'mandatory environmental tax R$ 150' — real Janauari Park entry R$ 25; (7) for travellers, the best value is the full-day GROUP tour from your Manaus hotel at R$ 300 — covers Encontro + Janauari + piranha fishing + village + lunch with safety infrastructure; (8) for photos, sit on the LEFT side of the boat on the outbound leg (Rio Negro is on your left facing downstream); (9) Dramamine 30 min before boarding — Amazonas river currents can be rough at the confluence line; (10) AMAZONASTUR +55 92 2123 8800 for operator verification; DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373.
scams.avoidance: Book group tour via Gero Tours / Viverde / Amazonastur R$ 250–R$ 400 per person VERIFY Marinha registration sticker BEFORE boarding; CHECK life jackets for every passenger REFUSE pink-dolphin swim (illegal IBAMA 2025) + helicopter upsell + 'mandatory R$ 150 tax' CONFIRM itinerary in writing: Encontro duration, Janauari activities, lunch, return time Dramamine 30 min pre-board; AMAZONASTUR +55 92 2123 8800; DEATUR +55 92 3584 1373
scams.location: Porto de Manaus + Ponta Negra pier + Marina David

scams.name: Centro Histórico & Mercado Adolpho Lisboa Pickpocket & Phone-Snatch Ring
scams.description: Manaus Centro Histórico (the 1890s rubber-boom colonial core — Teatro Amazonas, Largo de São Sebastião, Palácio Rio Negro, Mercado Adolpho Lisboa, Porto de Manaus) is the mandatory half-day tourist circuit, and hosts a documented 2025 pickpocket + phone-snatch pattern. Community reports cover 2025 Manaus safety, the 2025 Amazonas-region Uber-scam pattern, the 2026 Brazilian Carnaval anti-pickpocketing guide, 2025 solo-traveller advice, and broader Manaus community threads. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Teatro Amazonas square ('Largo de São Sebastião') phone-snatch — tourists take photos of the pink-and-blue opera house, a motorbike rider or pedestrian snatches the phone and runs through the adjacent calçadões; (b) Mercado Adolpho Lisboa (1883 cast-iron market, a Manaus landmark) crowded-aisle pickpocket — vendors' teams work with lookouts; during peak tourist hours (10 AM–noon and 3–5 PM) crowd-density lifts wallets + phones; (c) Porto de Manaus waterfront 'guide offer' — a 'helpful local' offers to show you the Encontro das Águas boat piers, steers you into a closed section, demands R$ 100 'tip'; (d) fake 'Teatro Amazonas guide R$ 80' on the front steps — the actual guided tour is R$ 20 purchased at the INSIDE ticket window (official 30-min tour in English); (e) aggressive vendor pressure at Palácio Rio Negro + Ponta Negra 'artisanal market' stalls — price-padding + bag rifling; (f) Centro-to-hotel walk at night (after 8 PM) — tourists walking back from dinner are targeted for phone-snatch + mugging on the quieter streets (Av. Eduardo Ribeiro, Rua 10 de Julho); (g) 'medical emergency' distraction at Largo de São Sebastião — older woman 'dizzy / blood pressure / call my son' while accomplice picks pocket; (h) Mercado Adolpho Lisboa 'samples' vendor pushing a piece of tambaqui fish or tucupi paste into your hand then demanding R$ 50. For travellers: (1) DO the Centro Histórico circuit DAYTIME ONLY (8 AM–5 PM), preferably 9 AM–noon when tourist police patrol visibility is highest; AVOID Centro after 6 PM entirely — Uber back to hotel from any dinner spot; (2) carry decoy phone + R$ 100 cash for the Centro walk; leave passport + cards + primary phone in hotel safe; (3) Teatro Amazonas photos: take quickly from the Largo de São Sebastião paving stones then STOW phone immediately — motorbike phone-snatch is documented; (4) for the Teatro Amazonas GUIDED TOUR, enter + pay R$ 20 at the INSIDE ticket window — official 30-min tours in English 9 AM / 11 AM / 2 PM / 4 PM; REFUSE every 'guide R$ 80' offer on the exterior steps; (5) Mercado Adolpho Lisboa: carry cross-body bag in FRONT; refuse every 'sample' push — if someone places food in your hand, drop it + walk away; the samples aren't free; (6) Porto de Manaus waterfront: stay with the main tour group / hotel-arranged boat — never follow a 'local guide' into a closed pier area; (7) if you see a 'medical emergency' approach, say 'I will call 192 (SAMU)' — exposes the scam instantly per São Paulo pattern; (8) for travellers, CONSIDER a half-day guided Centro Histórico tour via Amazonastur / Viverde at R$ 120–R$ 200 per person — licensed guide + safer group walk + accurate history; (9) DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373 (Tourist Police); Polícia Militar 190; SAMU 192.
scams.avoidance: Centro Histórico DAYTIME ONLY (9 AM–noon best); Uber back from any dinner spot Decoy phone + R$ 100 cash only; passport + cards + main phone in hotel safe Teatro Amazonas guided tour R$ 20 at INSIDE ticket window (9 AM / 11 AM / 2 PM / 4 PM English) Cross-body bag in FRONT at Mercado Adolpho Lisboa; refuse every 'sample' push DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373; Polícia Militar 190; SAMU 192
scams.location: Teatro Amazonas, Largo de São Sebastião, Mercado Adolpho Lisboa, Porto de Manaus

scams.name: Ponta Negra & Centro Restaurant Couvert + Serviço Padding & 'Peixe do Dia' Market-Price Trap
scams.description: Manaus dining corridors (Ponta Negra orla — the main tourist waterfront; Centro Histórico — around Teatro Amazonas + Largo de São Sebastião; Mercado Adolpho Lisboa — the cast-iron tambaqui + tucupi market) host the standard Brazilian tourist-restaurant overcharge pattern, with a distinctive Amazonian 'peixe do dia' (daily fish) market-price trap built around tambaqui, pirarucu, and tucunaré. Community reports cover 2025 Manaus safety and operator verification, broader dining mentions, 2025 solo-traveller advice, and the 2026 Brazilian Carnaval pattern. Brazilian restaurant law (Lei 13.419/2017) makes the 10% serviço charge OPTIONAL — you can refuse it, particularly for poor service. The 2025 scam patterns: (a) Ponta Negra orla 'couvert artístico R$ 80–R$ 150 per person' (legitimate R$ 15–R$ 35 for a genuine Amazonian musician — boi-bumbá, carimbó, forró); (b) 'peixe do dia preço de mercado' (daily fish market price) with no R$ per kg quoted — bill arrives R$ 280 for a 500g tambaqui fillet (real R$ 100–R$ 180 for same quantity); (c) 'pirarucu fresco R$ 350 mandatory weight' arrives as 900g serving billed R$ 850 (fair pirarucu is R$ 120–R$ 220 per kg, portion 400–500g is R$ 60–R$ 110); (d) 'tucunaré grelhado' at Ponta Negra barracas billed as 1kg when served 600g (weigh in front of you before cooking); (e) 'serviço 10%' added silently with the menu showing 'serviço opcional' fine print; (f) credit-card surcharge 5–10% only at bill-time ('we prefer PIX'); (g) Mercado Adolpho Lisboa food-stall 'tacacá gringo price' R$ 35 (local R$ 12) + 'tucupi shot R$ 15' (local R$ 4); (h) 'caldeirada de tambaqui para dois' at Ponta Negra restaurants served as portion for one, billed R$ 280 (fair R$ 120–R$ 180 for a genuine 2-person portion). For travellers: (1) BEFORE sitting, ask for the menu (carta) in Portuguese AND confirm in writing: (a) the couvert artístico R$ amount per person, (b) serviço 10% policy — photograph the menu page showing 'serviço opcional' (OPTIONAL under Lei 13.419/2017), (c) credit-card surcharge percentage; (2) for Amazonian fish, AGREE weight in R$ per kg IN WRITING BEFORE cooking — fair 2026 prices: tambaqui R$ 100–R$ 180 per kg, pirarucu R$ 120–R$ 220 per kg (pricier as it's a managed fishery), tucunaré R$ 80–R$ 150 per kg, matrinxã R$ 70–R$ 140 per kg; (3) reputable Ponta Negra restaurants: Banzeiro (Google 4.6+, Amazonian fine dining, R$ 120–R$ 280), Caxiri (riverside, R$ 80–R$ 180), Tambaqui de Banda (Ponta Negra barraca tradition, R$ 60–R$ 120); reputable Centro: Peixaria do Moraes (Centro Histórico, R$ 70–R$ 160), Mercado Adolpho Lisboa's upper-floor stalls (tacaça R$ 12–R$ 18 LOCAL PRICE); (4) AVOID English-only menus posted outside — walk 1–2 blocks inland for authentic local prices; (5) if serviço is added against your wishes for poor service, politely REFUSE and cite Lei 13.419/2017 — the manager knows this; (6) for Mercado Adolpho Lisboa food stalls, pay in Portuguese ('quanto é?') + small bills (R$ 10, R$ 20 notes); if a stall quotes you R$ 35 for tacacá, walk to the next stall — the next will be R$ 12; (7) for tucupi + tambaqui cooking demos at your hotel's partnered restaurant, confirm the R$ per kg BEFORE the demo starts; (8) PROCON Amazonas 151 for billing disputes; DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373.
scams.avoidance: BEFORE sitting, confirm couvert + serviço + card surcharge IN WRITING; photograph menu Fish: agree R$ per kg BEFORE cooking (tambaqui R$ 100–R$ 180/kg; pirarucu R$ 120–R$ 220/kg) Reputable: Banzeiro / Caxiri / Tambaqui de Banda (Ponta Negra); Peixaria do Moraes (Centro) REFUSE serviço if poor service (Lei 13.419/2017 — OPTIONAL); PROCON Amazonas 151 Mercado Adolpho Lisboa: pay in small bills + Portuguese; walk to next stall if gringo-priced
scams.location: Ponta Negra orla restaurants, Centro Histórico cafés, Mercado Adolpho Lisboa stalls

scams.name: Amazonas Regional Uber & Mototaxi Coordinated-Scam Pattern (Santarém / Alto do Chão Template)
scams.description: The broader Amazonas state (including side-trip destinations like Santarém, Alto do Chão, and Parintins) has a documented 2025 coordinated Uber / rideshare scam pattern that Manaus-based travellers encounter when venturing beyond the capital. Community reports document a team of drivers + passengers working together to defraud tourists via fake route detours, 'broken-meter' cash demands, and passport-card skimming. Manaus-parallel safety discussions, Amazon-context operator-verification threads, a regional Fortaleza app-scam pattern, and 2025 solo-traveller threads all reinforce the same defensive rules. The 2025 Santarém / Alto do Chão pattern (translatable to Manaus regional Uber and side-trips): (a) coordinated driver-passenger team — you book Uber, the app shows a driver 5 min away; en route to pickup, a passenger (planted accomplice) is already in the car; at pickup the driver claims 'another ride ahead of you' and asks you to wait or share — accomplice-passenger engages you in conversation while driver takes a 'shortcut' detour padding the fare; (b) 'meter / app failed — R$ 100 cash' demand mid-trip; (c) driver asking to 'see your card to confirm the Uber payment' — card skimming via hidden reader; (d) driver taking a deliberately long route to pad the in-app fare (Uber Brazil allows surge + long-route charges); (e) destination 'changed' — driver claims 'your hotel is closed' or 'that area is dangerous, I'll take you to a better hotel' — steering you to a commissioned 'safe' hotel that charges 3x normal rate; (f) in Parintins during Boi-Bumbá festival (June), rideshare supply collapses — unlicensed mototaxis + private-car drivers emerge charging 5–10x normal with robbery risk; (g) Alto do Chão river-beach day-trip: 'driver package R$ 600 round-trip + waiting' offered by airport tout — real Uber R$ 150–R$ 250 round-trip + hold on driver with hourly wait rate via in-app. For travellers: (1) ALWAYS verify driver name + car plate + photo MATCH the in-app profile BEFORE entering the vehicle — if mismatched, cancel + rebook; (2) NEVER share an Uber with an already-present 'other passenger' unless YOU explicitly booked UberPool — if a stranger is in the car on pickup, cancel in-app + report via safety button; (3) NEVER hand your credit or debit card to any driver for any reason — payment is ONLY via the in-app card or cash at the end of trip; refuse 'let me scan your card to confirm payment' demands; (4) FOLLOW the route on your phone's GPS (Google Maps in split-screen with Uber) — if the driver deviates significantly, ask 'está certo o caminho?' and if suspicious, ask to stop at the next public place (metro, mall, hotel) and cancel / rebook; (5) REFUSE every mid-trip 'meter broke, R$ 100 cash' demand — Uber Brazil uses GPS not a meter, the in-app price is final; if threatened, rule 911 / Polícia Militar 190; (6) if driver claims 'your hotel is closed / dangerous', tell them to take you to the original address or STOP immediately at the nearest public place — never let a stranger redirect your destination; (7) for Parintins Festival de Boi-Bumbá (late June), book transfers 3–6 months ahead via reputable operators; rideshare supply collapses during festival — do NOT plan last-minute mototaxi; (8) for Alto do Chão day-trip, book Uber round-trip with driver wait (via in-app 'Hora por hora' feature at R$ 40–R$ 60 per hour) — typical R$ 150–R$ 250 round-trip + R$ 200–R$ 300 wait for 6 hours = R$ 400–R$ 550; REFUSE every 'R$ 600 package' airport tout; (9) DEATUR Manaus +55 92 3584 1373; Polícia Militar 190; Uber in-app 24/7 safety line.
scams.avoidance: VERIFY driver name + plate + photo MATCH app BEFORE entering; cancel if mismatched NEVER share Uber with 'other passenger'; NEVER hand card to driver for any reason Follow GPS route on your phone; if deviation, demand stop at public place + cancel REFUSE every 'meter broke R$ 100 cash' mid-trip demand (Uber uses in-app GPS pricing) Book Parintins / Alto do Chão transfers via reputable operators 3–6 mo ahead; DEATUR +55 92 3584 1373
scams.location: Manaus Uber pickups + regional Amazonas Uber (Santarém, Alto do Chão, Parintins)
